source.title: 3DSeaVizKit: An interactive spatiotemporal visualization toolkit for ocean data
source.access_mode: Publisher-indexed full-text passage and Figure 11 caption returned by web search; direct page request returned HTTP 403. Original figure pixels and full PDF were not reviewed. The future issue label is retained as reported; no exact online publication date inferred.
source.source_locator: Gulf of Mexico application discussion immediately following Figure 11; Figure 11(a) caption.

reported_position.source_precision: approximately; printed latitude has one decimal place and longitude is a whole degree

identity_context.naming_support: The source explicitly names both Nautilus I and Nautilus II and places the latter near 24.5 N, 92 W on May 26. It separately locates the parent Nautilus near 26 N, 90 W and Michael near 25.5 N, 94.5 W.
identity_context.branch_stage: Splitting branch on May 26; the source says it is fully detached by June 6. This does not establish an exact split date or observed physical birth.

diagnostic.product: A separate native daily DUACS ADT field on the nominal source date, not the MSEAS velocity/vorticity simulation or direct observations.

haley_2023_archive.decision: The archived payload is truncated at 5 MiB, has no terminal EOF marker and produces missing-object and truncated-image warnings. No dimensions, point or complete figure interpretation taken from it.

he_slide.decision: Charts name Lazarus, Michael and parent Nautilus; no separately legible Nautilus II size or boundary admitted. The final chart says May 9 while its overlaid slide label says May 1; no date substitution.

horizon_public_example.decision: The public sample labels only Warm Eddy and has no map date. Archive capture date is not an observation date; no named identity or size assigned.
